account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: a morning market walk, lunch at home, town accounts at thirteen, and now tea with the neighbour at the east-bank cottage. Several residents told me they had no news. I checked the treasury and saw 128 emeralds; the secretary says no bills, council papers, or correspondence have reached her. She personally confirmed this tea address. I arrived just before fifteen, and the neighbour has welcomed me and asked about my day and town-hall news.

The main new business is the innkeeper's request for a meeting tomorrow at eighteen in the great hall about the inn's service to town. I agreed and asked the secretary to record it. The innkeeper intends to meet me at my office at seventeen forty-five and walk there with me. That escort is a specific arrangement worth remembering, but I have heard nothing establishing any purpose beyond the stated discussion of the inn's service.

During the market walk I also heard Townsfolk 08 and 18 asking the builder for an update on town works. I have not heard an answer or learned of any particular problem. Nothing I have directly observed establishes an emergency or unusual disturbance. I should hear what the neighbour knows about the riverside, then return to the office for sixteen thirty.
